title: What is Collectors.mapping used for as a downstream collector (transform elements within each group)?
keyPoints: Collectors.mapping(mapper, downstream) transforms elements WITHIN each group before collecting
groupingBy(dept, mapping(getName, toList())) produces Map<String, List<String>> instead of Map<String, List<Employee>>
mapping composes with any inner collector: toList, toSet, joining, reducing, counting
Without mapping, groupingBy always collects the original objects into each group
mapping is the downstream equivalent of the stream map() operation
Use mapping when you need to extract or transform a field within each group in a single collect call

s1_definition.oneliner: Collectors.mapping applies a transformation to each element within a group before the downstream collector processes it, letting you group by one field but collect a different projected value.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **mapping(mapper, downstream)** transforms elements within each group before collecting.
- **groupingBy(classifier, mapping(extractor, toList()))** groups by one attribute but collects a different projected value per group.
- Without mapping: `groupingBy(department)` gives `Map<String, List<Employee>>` (whole objects).
- With mapping: `groupingBy(department, mapping(getName, toList()))` gives `Map<String, List<String>>` (just names).
- mapping composes with any inner collector: `toList()`, `toSet()`, `joining(", ")`, `reducing(...)`, `counting()`.
- It is the downstream equivalent of the `map()` intermediate operation.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, groupingBy department gives you departments mapped to lists of full employee records. But the branch summary only needs names, not complete records. mapping extracts just the name from each employee before collecting, like a clerk who copies only the name column from each full form into the summary report.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  accounts stream
       │
       ▼
  groupingBy(branch)
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ MUMBAI:  [Account(Rajesh), Account(Priya)] │
  │ DELHI:   [Account(Amit), Account(Kavita)]  │
  │ CHENNAI: [Account(Suresh)]                 │
  └──────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                     │
                     ▼
  mapping(Account::holder, toList())
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ MUMBAI:  ["Rajesh", "Priya"]               │
  │ DELHI:   ["Amit", "Kavita"]                │
  │ CHENNAI: ["Suresh"]                        │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Collectors.mapping is a downstream collector that transforms elements within each group before the inner downstream processes them. `groupingBy(branch, mapping(holder, toList()))` groups by branch and collects holder NAMES instead of full Account objects.

It composes with any inner collector: toList for lists, toSet for unique values, joining for CSV strings, reducing for aggregation. Without mapping, groupingBy always collects the original objects.

At National Bank of India, the branch summary maps each branch to a comma-separated list of account holder names using `mapping(holder, joining(", "))` in a single collect call.

Remember one sentence: mapping inside groupingBy extracts and transforms a field within each group, like map() but scoped to each group.
